title: Reusing previously created geom_mark_hull() layer without recalculating?
description:
Thanks for the really nice package! I read in the documentation that "The hull is calculated at draw time, and can thus change as you resize the plot". I was wondering if there could be an easy way to reuse a previously calculated hull layer while overriding the recalculation, for instance when aiming at plotting the exact same hull over the same collection of points with an underlying layer that is changing. Below is a toy example of what I am trying to achieve. Here, `plotDF` would be a data frame with coordinates `X`/`Y` for points in a square grid, with each of these points having intensities `Z` for a set of different variables `Var`, and some (but not all) of these points in turn being univocally assigned to certain regions (specified by the column `Region`).

```
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)

hullDF <- plotDF[,c("X","Y","Region")] %>% filter(!is.na(Region)) %>% distinct()   # Unique X/Y/Region triplets
ggHull <- geom_mark_hull(data = hullDF, aes(x = X, y = Y, group = Region))         # Create hull layer before loop

for (V in unique(plotDF$Var)) {
    ggRasterAndHull <- ggplot(data = subset(plotDF, Var==V)) +
                       geom_raster(aes(x = X, y = Y, fill = Z)) +
                       ggHull    # Create raster for variable "V" overlaid with hull
    print(ggRasterAndHull )
}
```

The issue I find is that, as mentioned in the documentation, the hull layer gets recalculated at every iteration (I assume upon the call `print()`?), which in this case would not really be necessary, but takes the most time out of all the steps in the loop.

Thanks a lot for any guidance/hints you can provide!

title: geom_mark_ellipse renders incorrect ellipse orientation with 3-point groups
description: geom_mark_ellipse renders ellipses with a wrong orientation for certain 3-point group configurations. The ellipse appears to have the correct shape but is displaced/mirrored vertically, suggesting a sign error in the coordinate transformation rather than a failure of the Khachiyan algorithm itself. This may be related to issue #214? **Reproducible example:** ``` library(ggplot2) library(ggforce) bug_data <- data.frame( PC1 = c(-1.33, 92.6, 78.5), PC2 = c(46.5, -22.4, 0.9) ) ggplot(bug_data, aes(PC1, PC2)) + geom_point(size = 3) + ggforce::geom_mark_ellipse(aes(fill = "D"), alpha = 0.3) # expanded view to draw whole ellipse ggplot(bug_data, aes(PC1, PC2)) + geom_point(size = 3) + ggforce::geom_mark_ellipse(aes(fill = "D"), alpha = 0.3) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-50, 150), ylim = c(-100, 100)) ``` A quick manual Khachiyan implementation (made with Claude) shows an ellipse that correctly encloses all points and is indeed a vertical mirror of the geom_mark_ellipse ellipse. > **Session info** > R: 4.4.1 (2024-06-14 ucrt) > Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 > ggforce_0.5.0 > ggplot2_4.0.1

title: geom_mark_*() errors in webR when description is missing
description:
Hi Thomas 👋  

Hope you’re well! 

We’ve run into something odd with `geom_mark_*()` and wanted to check whether this is expected behavior or a small edge case. And if there is anythoing we are missing and potential ways to fix it (either from oru or your side).

In webR-based environments, which we’re using in-browser sandboxes in our uncharted course, `geom_mark_*()` (e.g. `geom_mark_circle()) throws:

```
Error: Problem while converting geom to grob.
```

This happens whenever a `description` is not porivded. What’s surprising is that the error completely disappears as soon as any character string is provided for the description.

---

🔁 Minimal example

This fails in webR:

```r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)

ggplot(
    data = penguins,
    aes(x = flipper_len, y = body_mass, fill = species)
) +
    geom_mark_ellipse(aes(label = species)) +
    geom_point(shape = 21, size = 2)
```

This works:

```r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)

ggplot(
    data = penguins,
    aes(x = flipper_len, y = body_mass, fill = species)
) +
    geom_mark_ellipse(aes(label = species, description = "")) + # empty quotes for description make it work
    geom_point(shape = 21, size = 2)
```

---

Our hypothesis after doing some research: the grob tree constructed by `geom_mark_*()` is incomplete when `description` is missing, and webR’s graphics device is stricter about validating grobs. In a full desktop R session, this seems to slip through unnoticed, but in webR it fails hard.

If that's the reason: 
Would it be possible for `geom_mark_*()` to return a complete grob structure, even when description is not supplied, so it behaves consistently across devices?

Thanks a lot for ggforce and all your other packages 🙌

title: Bug: NA in data messes up geom_mark_*() label placement
Customizing date labels in facet_zoom
description:
I have a daily timeseries for one year and want to make a zoomed out plot that shows the whole timeseries and a zoomed in plot on a few specific dates. For the zoomed out plot, I want the x-axis to show the month and year stacked on top of one another, which can be achieved using `scale_x_date(date_labels = '%b\n%Y')`. However, in the zoomed in plot, I want to show month and day. I am trying to do this using `ggforce::facet_zoom()` but it seems to inherit the date_labels from scale_x_date. How can I customize the date labels when using `facet_zoom`?

The ideal output would have the zoomed out plot with `date_labels = '%b\n%Y'` and the zoomed in plot would have `date_labels = '%b %d'`

``` r
library(tidyverse)
library(ggforce)

# Example data
dat <- data.frame(
  date = seq(as.Date('2024-01-01'),
             as.Date('2024-12-31'),
             '1 day'),
  value = rnorm(366, 10, 3)
)

# Plot 1: without setting date_labels, the default is to show the month and year while the zoomed plot shows month and day
dat |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = value)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = 'Value') +
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
  facet_zoom(xlim = c(as.Date("2024-06-01"), as.Date("2024-06-20")))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/9BPmrRv.png)<!-- -->

``` r
# Plot 2: when I set the date_labels for the zoomed out plot, the day no longer shows in the zoomed in plot
dat |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = value)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_date(breaks = seq(as.Date('2024-01-01'),
                            as.Date('2024-12-31'),
                            '1 month'),
               limits = c(as.Date('2024-01-01'),
                          as.Date('2024-12-31')),
               date_labels = '%b\n%Y') +
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = 'Value') +
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
  facet_zoom(xlim = c(as.Date("2024-06-01"), as.Date("2024-06-20")))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/F3FK9s0.png)<!-- -->

<sup>Created on 2025-08-13 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

I have also asked this question on [stack overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79734728/ggforce-how-to-customize-date-labels-in-facet-zoom).

description:

title: Allow facet_col() to accept a data parameter
description:
Hi 👋,

I’d like to suggest a feature that would make `facet_col()` more flexible: adding a data parameter, similar to how it works in `ggplot()` or `geom_*()` layers.

## Motivation

Currently, `facet_col()` does not accept a data argument, so the faceting variable must exist in the main data passed to `ggplot()`. This can be limiting when:

- The variable you'd like to facet by exists in a separate data frame

- You’re layering multiple data sources in a single plot

While it is possible to work around this by joining the data frames beforehand, being able to directly specify `data = df` inside `facet_col()` would streamline this process and align better with tidyverse-style workflows.

## Example (Currently not possible):

```
ggplot(df1, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_col(data = df2, vars(group))
```

This currently throws an error since facet_col() does not support a data parameter.

## Proposed Behavior

Support for `data = ...` in `facet_col()` (and possibly in `facet_row()` as well), with internal handling that merges or references the appropriate facetting structure without requiring manual pre-joins.

Thank you for considering this!

title: Unnecessary offset in place_labels?
description:
Hi,

I was trying to figure out, why I can't get more compact labeling in https://github.com/thomasp85/ggforce/issues/333, and noticed that there seem to be an unnecessary offset in `place_labels` function (https://github.com/thomasp85/ggforce/blob/main/R/mark_label.R#L70):

```r
polygons[[length(polygons) + 1]] <- polyoffset(rect, 10)
```

As far as I understand, it creates and additional space around the label. However, `rects` already accounts for `label.margin`, so I don't understand what's the point of an additional offset. Changing the offset from 10 to 0 greatly improved the label positioning for me.

--
Alexey

title: Grouping by variable in geom_link2 throws error
description:
With `ggplot2::geom_path`, setting `group = _y_` in the aesthetic mapping connects observations with the same value for _y_. For example, I am visualizing the paths taken by agents in a 2D environment, where I want to stratify paths by a unique agent ID. However, when I try to to use this argument in `geom_link2` I receive the error:

```
Warning message:
Computation failed in `stat_link2()`.
Caused by error in `data.frame()`:
! arguments imply differing number of rows: 2, 0
```

A minimal working example using the reference:

```
lines <- data.frame(
  x = c(5, 12, 15, 9, 6),
  y = c(17, 20, 4, 15, 5),
  xend = c(19, 17, 2, 9, 5),
  yend = c(10, 18, 7, 12, 1),
  width = c(1, 10, 6, 2, 3),
  group = c("a", "a", "b", "b", "c")

 ggplot(lines) +
     geom_link2(aes(x = x, y = y, colour = colour, size = width, group = group),
                lineend = 'round', n = 500)
)
```

In fact, this works when setting `group` to any of the columns. It seems to work only if there are at least 2 observation in each group and the same number of observations across groups (2 <= N_i == N_(-i)).

Is this expected, and is there a way to achieve groups as in `geom_path`?

title: Enable Operation on Lists of Plots
Possible bug in makeContent.shape when expand, radius= 0
description:
I'm trying to use the new shapeGrob export on the "experiment-rounded-rect" branch of hughjonesd/ggmagnify. I ran into an error, which I now can't reproduce, like this:

```r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggmagnify)

ggp <- ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Width, Sepal.Length, color = Species, shape = Species))
ggp2 <- ggp + geom_point()

from <- c(2.5, 3.0, 5.5, 6.0)
to <- c(3.5, 4.5, 4.5, 5.5)
ggp2 + geom_magnify(from = from, to = to, corners = 0.05)
```

`corners` is passed into the `radius` argument to `shapeGrob`.

This did give the error:

```r
Error in p$x : $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors
```
though now it seems to be ok :-/


Anyway, it seemed to happen when the `radius` and `expand` variables in `makeContent.shape` evaluated to 0 via the code in `convertWidth` (perhaps because of a small viewport?) If so, then the various `polyoffset` functions in `makeContent.shape` aren't called, and then the `polygons` variable ends up not set up correctly for some reason.

I'm sorry, this isn't a very useful bug report! But you might be able to understand what's happened better than me and work out a test case for this code path.

title: Feature request: add label_colour as an aesthetic
description:
Hello,
Thank you for a very useful package. 

It would be handy to be able to map `label.colour` to the data as an aesthetic. As an example:

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, col = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point() +
  ggforce::geom_mark_ellipse(aes(label = cyl)) 
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/7bFMijK.png)

<sup>Created on 2021-06-11 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

Here it would be useful to colour the 4, 6, and 8 labels the same as the points and ellipses, by mapping them to the data. 

We can colour _all_ annotations:

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, col = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point() +
  ggforce::geom_mark_ellipse(aes(label = cyl),
                             label.colour = "red") 
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/hjlq7rY.png)

<sup>Created on 2021-06-11 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

But `label.colour` is not implemented as an aesthetic: 

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, col = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point() +
  ggforce::geom_mark_ellipse(aes(label = cyl,
                                 label.colour = cyl)) 
#> Warning: Ignoring unknown aesthetics: label.colour
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/zxbVBBr.png)

<sup>Created on 2021-06-11 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.0)</sup>

Making `label.colour` an aesthetic would be a really useful addition to the package.

title: [feature request] geom_subplot
description:
[`ggsubplot`](https://github.com/garrettgman/ggsubplot) has been [deprecated](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ggsubplot/index.html) for years, but tidyverse support for [list columns](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/group_nest.html) and [custom annotations](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/annotation_custom.html) in `ggplot2` make it pretty easy to mimic its functionality. However, there is some boilerplate logic that I could see fitting into a new geom, i.e. `geom_subplot()`.

First, some examples on how to embed plots in a plot:

```r
# simple example (unlikely use case -- could instead use facet_grid) 
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)

titanic = as.data.frame(Titanic, responseName = "value") %>%
  group_nest(Class, Sex) %>%
  mutate(
    Class = factor(Class),
	Sex = factor(Sex),
	X = as.integer(Class),
	Y = as.integer(Sex),
    plot = map(data, 
	  ~ggplot(.x) + geom_col(aes(x = Survived, y = value))
	),
	annotation = pmap(list(X, Y, plot),
      ~ annotation_custom(ggplotGrob(..3),
        xmin = ..1 - 0.4, xmax = ..1 + 0.4,
        ymin = ..2 - 0.4, ymax = ..2 + 0.4))
  )
ggplot(titanic) + aes(x = Class, y = Sex) + geom_point() + pull(titanic, annotation)
```
![plot1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4790348/59121176-3a2ab100-890c-11e9-8884-1c508cd503a7.png)

```r
# mapping example (more likely use case)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)

nc <- st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"))
data(Crime, package = "Ecdat")

ncdat = nc %>%
  st_transform(3857) %>%
  bind_cols(as_tibble(st_coordinates(st_centroid(.))))

crimedat = Crime %>% 
  group_nest(county) %>%
  inner_join(select(st_drop_geometry(ncdat), X, Y, CRESS_ID), by = c("county" = "CRESS_ID")) %>%
  mutate(
    plot = map(data, ~ggplot(.x) + aes(x = year, y = crmrte) + geom_line(color = "red") + theme_void()),
	annotation = pmap(list(X, Y, plot), ~ annotation_custom(ggplotGrob(..3),
      xmin = ..1 - 8000 , xmax = ..1 + 8000,
      ymin = ..2 - 8000 , ymax = ..2 + 8000)) 
  )
    
ggplot(ncdat) + geom_sf() + pull(crimedat, annotation)
```
![plot2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4790348/59121257-75c57b00-890c-11e9-96a3-96de851a21a1.png)

And here's a more sophisticated example ([link to blog plost with code](https://hydroecology.net/a-ggsubplot-revival/)).

![plot3](https://hydroecology.net/images/salinitymaps.svg)

I'm thinking a `geom_subplot()` could handle the last step of transforming a list of plots into custom annotations, replacing the final call to `pmap` and manual addition of the annotation list to the base plot in the above examples. In other words, the geom would take a dataframe with a list column containing `ggplot` objects and map them onto the "base" plot. This would provide maximum flexibility for users generating the suplots themselves and avoid a lot of the messy aesthetics that was in `ggsubplot`. The new geom would accept subplot locations, dimensions, and the subplots themselves (i.e. `geom_subplot(aes(x, y, height, width, plot))`). At the same time, the new geom could provide helper arguments to 
- ignore missing or empty subplots
- apply standardized axis limits, font sizes, themes, and `theme` options
- expand the axis limits of the base plot (since `annotation_custom` does not affect scales)
- potentially assist creating a unified legends and drop legends from individual subplots
- potentially make a good guess of reasonable subplot `height` and `width` based on the extent of base plot

I've been learning more about extending ggplot2 and would be interested in helping develop this functionality, but I don't think I have the necessary expertise to develop this on my own. I also would prefer to contribute to `ggforce` rather than try to maintain a separate package, since `ggforce` clearly has a well-developed underlying framework for developing new geoms.

title: Add scale_color_units to allow for units in continous color scales.
description:
It would be great if continuous color scales could also have units.

Example:

```
library(ggplot2)
library(units)
library(ggforce)

# Plot looks great without units:
ggplot(iris, aes(x=Sepal.Length, y=Sepal.Width, color = Petal.Length)) + 
  geom_point()

# Adding units to the dataset
iris$Sepal.Length =  set_units(iris$Sepal.Length, cm)
iris$Sepal.Width  =  set_units(iris$Sepal.Width,  cm)
iris$Petal.Length =  set_units(iris$Petal.Length, cm)
iris$Petal.Width  =  set_units(iris$Petal.Width,  cm)

ggplot(iris, aes(x=Sepal.Length, y=Sepal.Width, color = Petal.Length)) + 
  geom_point()

```

The ggplot with units in the color aesthetic causes the following error:
```
Error in Ops.units(x, range[1]) : 
  both operands of the expression should be "units" objects
```

Thanks :)

title: Radius for geom_shape only on alternate corners
description:
Is there a way to make the radius argument in geom_shape to apply to both 'inside' and 'outside' corners of a shape? When something like a step shape is used, only alternate corners get rounded. It seems like the curve for the shape needs to be able to both expand and contract from the basic shape to get curves on every step:

```
test <- tibble(x = c(.5, 1.5, 1.5, 2.5, 2.5, 3.5, 3.5, 4.5, 4.5, 5.5, 5.5, .5,
             4.5, 4.5, 5.5, 5.5, 6.5, 6.5, 7.5, 7.5, 8.5, 8.5, 9.5, 9.5, 10.5, 10.5, 11.5, 11.5, 12.5, 12.5, 11.5, 11.5, 10.5, 10.5),
       y = c(9, 9, 7, 7, 5, 5, 3, 3, 1, 1, 0, 0,
             15, 13, 13, 11, 11, 9, 9, 7, 7, 5, 5, 3, 3, 1, 1, 0, 0, 11, 11, 13, 13, 15),
       id = c(rep("a", 12),
              rep("b", 22)))

ggplot(data = test) +
  geom_shape(aes(x = x, y = y, group = id), fill = "grey50", linetype = "blank", alpha = .1, radius = unit(8, "points"))
```

title: Easy way to split one field into n facets
description:
I often create a heat map that is too long to display on one chart. I have to scratch my head each time to figure out how to break it into columns. I eventually end up with some integer division solution `x %/% y` like here:
Code ```r library(tidyverse) library(scales) df <- USJudgeRatings |> as_tibble(rownames = "y") |> gather(x, fill, -y) |> mutate( x = fct_reorder(x, fill, mean), y = fct_reorder(y, fill, sum, .desc = FALSE) ) |> print() # number of columns for plot n_col <- 2 # separate into columns and keep factor order plot_prep <- df |> mutate( y_order = as.integer(y), max_rows = ceiling(n_distinct(y) / n_col), facets = (-y_order %/% max_rows) # needs something to facet on, need '-' to keep highest values on left ) |> print() # plot p <- plot_prep |> ggplot(aes(x, y, fill = fill)) + facet_wrap(~facets, ncol = n_col, scales = "free_y") + geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.5) + scale_fill_stepsn(breaks = breaks_pretty(6), colours = viridis_pal()(5)) + theme( strip.background.y = element_blank(), strip.text = element_blank(), axis.text = element_text(size = 7) ) p + theme(aspect.ratio = 1) # identify aspect ratio aspect <- plot_prep |> select(x, y) |> summarise_all(n_distinct) |> mutate(ratio = y / x / n_col) |> print() p + theme(aspect.ratio = aspect$ratio) # <------ fixed 1:1 size ```
Could a solution be implemented like one of these? * `facet_wrap(facets = ~., ncol = 2)` -- currently just keeps chart as-is (no facets) * a helper function `facet_wrap(facets = split_facet(ncol = 2))` * a new function `facet_split(ncol = 2)` --- Additionally, I often struggle to get the ratios correct. `coord_fixed()` throws an error and `aspect.ratio` affects each panel rather than "unit of y per unit of x". I included code ☝️ to show how I do it: `[# unique y] / [# unique x] / [# of cols]` I originally posted in the ggplot2 repo https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/4763 but was directed to work with other package creators who might be able to take this on. I :heart: `ggforce` and think it could be a good home for this type of faceting.

title: `geom_circle` appearance in legend
description:
Sorry - I know this is not a bug, but I'd like your opinion on it anyway. The reprex below shows how I would use `geom_circle` to draw a circle around some but not all `geom_point`. As far as I know, the legend will always show a rectanlge around the symbols, yet it would be nice if it would actually be a circle. I don't think I can approach this with `guide()` or `theme(legend.key = )`. Can you think of a solution?

``` r
library(ggforce)

dat <- data.frame(
  x = c(1, 1.3, 1.6),
  y = c(1, 1, 1),
  circle = c("yes", "no", "no")
)

ggplot() +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_classic() +
  geom_circle(
    data = subset(dat, circle == "yes"),
    aes(x0 = x, y0 = y, r = 0.5, alpha = circle),
    fill = "grey",
    color = NA,
    show.legend = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = dat,
    aes(x, y, color = circle)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("yes" = "blue", "no" = "red")
  ) +
  scale_alpha_manual(
    values = c("yes" = 0.25, "no" = 0)
  )
```

title: Feature request: standalone geom_mark
description:
Huge fan of the appearance and functionality behind the annotation style used in geom_mark_ellipse() and the other geoms that allow both a label and description, and would really like in some instances to be able to force where they appear, or use them without needing to reference datapoints you wish to mark. 

This would be particularly helpful in cases when using multiple geom_mark_ellipse() lines to either highlight different subsets of data or when the data comes from different dataframes. Oftentimes these labels will overlay other data when employing filters and it would be good to have controls against that outside of building the descriptions into the dataframes themselves. Would also be helpful when standardizing placement for reproducible reporting.

# Example use case highlighting the current implementation
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, col = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point() +
  ggforce::geom_mark_ellipse(aes(filter = cyl == 4,
                                 label = cyl),
                             description = "4 Cyllinders are okay")  +
  ggforce::geom_mark_ellipse(aes(filter = cyl == 6,
                                 label = cyl),
                             description = "6 Cyllinders are equally okay too") 


![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33760885/192318454-ddaf76cb-102a-40d4-b028-92ab44d39094.png)

# Potential functionality
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, col = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point() +
  ggforce::geom_mark_ellipse(aes(filter = cyl == 4,
                                 label = cyl),
                             description = "4 Cyllinders are okay")  +
  ggforce::geom_mark_text(
    con.x = 3.5,
    con.y = 28,
    label.x = 4,
    label.y = 32,
    label = "6"
    description = "I want my 6 cyllinder label over here, I don't care where my plot window thinks it should go")

title: Error in `facet_zoom()` while using `theme_set()` and `ggthemes`
description:
I was trying to plot something using `facet_zoom()` with `xlim` to specify the region and was getting "subscript too long..." error. I tried the vanilla example from the docs and I got the same error.

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)
theme_set(ggthemes::theme_base() + theme(plot.background = element_rect(color=NA)))
ggplot(iris, aes(Petal.Length, Petal.Width, colour = Species)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_zoom(xlim = c(2, 4))
#> Warning in rep(colour, length.out = length(alpha)): 'x' is NULL so the result
#> will be NULL
#> Error in `[<-`(`*tmp*`, !is.na(alpha), 4, value = alpha[!is.na(alpha)]): (subscript) logical subscript too long
```

I knew that the vanilla example had to work, so I tried it using `theme_gray()`  and it woks as expected.

```
# Works with theme gray()
ggplot(iris, aes(Petal.Length, Petal.Width, colour = Species)) +
  geom_point() + 
  theme_gray() +
  facet_zoom(xlim = c(2, 4)) 
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/ddXjniZ.png)

Same for `theme_bw()`

``` r
# Works with theme bw()
ggplot(iris, aes(Petal.Length, Petal.Width, colour = Species)) +
  geom_point() + 
  theme_bw() +
  facet_zoom(xlim = c(2, 4)) 
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/UtT1ajJ.png)

Not sure this is a `ggforce` or `ggthemes` issue to be honest, so this might not be the best place to put it.

title: `geom_circle()` and `geom_ellipse()` do not handle `linewidth` aesthetic properly
description:
Since ggplot 3.4.0 `size` was replaced with `linewidth`, but it seems like `geom_circle()` and `geom_ellipse()` don't properly respect this change. As it ignores linewidth outside of `aes()` and raises lifecycle warning.

See code below
``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)

ggplot() +
  geom_ellipse(
    aes(x0 = 0, y0 = 0, a = 10, b = 3, angle = 0),
    linewidth = 5
  ) +
  coord_fixed()
#> Warning in geom_ellipse(aes(x0 = 0, y0 = 0, a = 10, b = 3, angle = 0), linewidth
#> = 5): Ignoring unknown parameters: `linewidth`
#> Warning: Using the `size` aesthetic in this geom was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0.
#> ℹ Please use `linewidth` in the `default_aes` field and elsewhere instead.
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/2lphERf.png)<!-- -->

``` r

ggplot() +
  geom_circle(
    aes(x0 = 0, y0 = 0, r = 10),
    linewidth = 5
  ) +
  coord_fixed()
#> Warning in geom_circle(aes(x0 = 0, y0 = 0, r = 10), linewidth = 5): Ignoring
#> unknown parameters: `linewidth`
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/4VURokx.png)<!-- -->

<sup>Created on 2022-11-23 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

It is, however, possible to control linewidth inside `aes()`, but it also raises warnings:

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)

ggplot() +
  geom_circle(
    aes(x0 = 0, y0 = 0, r = 10,
        linewidth = I(3)),
  ) +
  coord_fixed()
#> Warning in geom_circle(aes(x0 = 0, y0 = 0, r = 10, linewidth = I(3)), ):
#> Ignoring unknown aesthetics: linewidth
#> Warning: Using the `size` aesthetic in this geom was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0.
#> ℹ Please use `linewidth` in the `default_aes` field and elsewhere instead.
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/MIyYquc.png)<!-- -->

title: facet_wrap_paginate(): dropping colors in the legend
description:
Hello,

Thank you for a very nice package! I found function facet_wrap_paginate() especially useful, but would be great if it would also allow for dropping irrelevant colors from the legend..

As an example: here is a plot using **starwars** dataset from **dplyr** package, where I want to assign a specific color to every name.
```
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)
library(dplyr)

plot_data <- starwars[1:20, ]
g <- ggplot(data = plot_data, aes(x = homeworld, y = height, color = name)) + 
  geom_point(size = 3) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#89C5DA", "#DA5724", "#74D944", "#CE50CA", "#3F4921", "#C0717C", "#CBD588", "#5F7FC7", 
                                         "#673770", "#D3D93E", "#38333E", "#508578", "#D7C1B1", "#689030", "#AD6F3B", "#CD9BCD", 
                                         "#D14285", "#6DDE88", "#652926", "#7FDCC0"),
                     labels = unique(plot_data$name)) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))
```

Then I use facet_wrap_paginate() function to have at most 6 facets per page:

`g + facet_wrap_paginate(facets = "hair_color", nrow = 3, ncol = 2, page = 1)`

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37506232/224568620-6b5c4043-9461-4bf9-8997-4e4a772b6309.png)

And then the second page:
`g + facet_wrap_paginate(facets = "hair_color", nrow = 3, ncol = 2, page = 2)`
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/37506232/224568650-228e0cbb-a8d0-45d4-9cb5-c5b3807e3f06.png)

As you can see, color legend on both pages is the same, even though the names in the dataset are unique and are only present on one of the two pages. It would be handy to have an option to drop those irrelevant elements from the legend.

description: I've been trying to make a reproducible version of a diagram of the sampling scheme for a particular field project, mirroring this version that I made by hand in PowerPoint: Geom_mark_rect has been super helpful for creating boxes around the collections of points. However, I've been having trouble making the boxes fit more tightly around the points (and not being forced to squares); when I try to make a similarly narrow version of the R figure, the boxes overlap: It would be great if there were a way to make the geom_mark_rect boxes tighter around the points; any advice on parameters to change or things to try would be greatly appreciated. The code used to produce the R figure is below, where data_forchart can be imported from the attached .csv: ``` facet.labs = c("Tide Pool 1\n (S1)", "Tide Pool 2\n (S2)", "Nearshore\n (N)") names(facet.labs) = c("S1", "S2", "N") data_forchart$Location= factor(data_forchart$Location, levels=c("S1", "S2", "N")) data_forchart$chart_num= factor(data_forchart$chart_num, levels=c("3", "2", "1")) sample_schema = ggplot(data = data_forchart, aes(x = Time, y = chart_num, shape = Location, color = Time, fill = Time)) + geom_beeswarm(cex= 2, size = 3) + geom_mark_rect(expand = .03) + scale_shape_manual(values = c(15, 17, 16)) + viridis::scale_color_viridis(discrete=TRUE, begin = 0, end = .97, direction = -1) + viridis::scale_fill_viridis(discrete=TRUE, begin = 0, end = .97, direction = -1) + facet_grid(Location ~., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y", labeller = labeller(Location = facet.labs)) + theme_void(base_size = 16) + theme(legend.position = "none") + theme(strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, vjust = .9)) ``` [Chart_Data.csv](https://github.com/thomasp85/ggforce/files/11971114/Chart_Data.csv) [28-Jan-2022-TideChart.txt](https://github.com/thomasp85/ggforce/files/12074519/28-Jan-2022-TideChart.txt)

title: `GeomLine` support for `stat_link2` + other interpolation methods
description:
Currently, the `stat_link*` family plots paths, but it would be great to have a version that works like `GeomLine` (i.e., drawn by along the x-value), or at least support for mixing with `GeomLine`:

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)

lines <- data.frame(
  x = c(5, 12, 15, 9, 6),
  y = c(17, 20, 4, 15, 5),
  xend = c(19, 17, 2, 9, 5),
  yend = c(10, 18, 7, 12, 1),
  width = c(1, 10, 6, 2, 3),
  colour = letters[1:5]
)
```

default `geom_link2` stat and geom:

``` r
ggplot(lines, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = colour, size = width, group = 1)) +
  layer(stat = StatLink2, geom = ggforce:::GeomPathInterpolate,
        position = position_identity(),
        params = list(n = 500, lineend = 'round'))
#> Warning: Using `size` aesthetic for lines was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0.
#> ℹ Please use `linewidth` instead.
#> This warning is displayed once every 8 hours.
#> Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was
#> generated.
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/TCbLJg7.png)<!-- -->

doesn’t work with `GeomLine`:

``` r
ggplot(lines, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = colour, size = width, group = 1)) +
  layer(stat = StatLink2, geom = GeomLine,
        position = position_identity(),
        params = list(n = 10, lineend = 'round'))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/rgw5PYq.png)<!-- -->

sorting by x doesn’t solve it:

``` r
dplyr::arrange(lines, x) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y, colour = colour, size = width, group = 1)) +
  layer(stat = StatLink2, geom = GeomLine,
        position = position_identity(),
        params = list(n = 10, lineend = 'round'))
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/mvq3e2p.png)<!-- -->

<sup>Created on 2023-10-25 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

---

Additionally, if a "GeomLine" like behavior is supported, adding more interpolation variants would allow for drawing spline interpolated lines, and others.

For example:

``` r
xout <- seq(min(lines$x), max(lines$x), len = 50)
y_linear <- approx(lines$x, lines$y, xout = xout)[["y"]]
y_spline <- spline(lines$x, lines$y, xout = xout)[["y"]]

lines_interp <- data.frame(x = xout, y_linear, y_spline)

ggplot(lines_interp, aes(x)) + 
  # geom_link2(aes(y = y), data = lines, stat = GeomPath)
  geom_line(aes(y = y_linear, color = "linear")) + 
  geom_line(aes(y = y_spline, color = "spline")) + 
  geom_point(aes(y = y), data = lines, size = 3)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/nVu0xFT.png)<!-- -->

<sup>Created on 2023-10-25 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

Thanks!

title: Order of geom_edge_link plotting does not match order of input data for more than 9 edges
description:
When using `geom_edge_link()`, sorting the input graph edges does not have the expected effect on the plotting order of those edges (in particular when the number of edges is greater than 9). 

``` r
library(tidyverse)
library(tidygraph)
library(ggraph)

# create a toy graph
g <- tbl_graph(edges=tibble(from=1:12, to=13:24), directed=FALSE) %E>%
  mutate(z=1:n()) %N>%
  mutate(type=c(rep(TRUE, 12), rep(FALSE, 12)))

# standardize layout for comparisons (and so that edges cross)
layout <- igraph::layout_as_bipartite(g) %>%
  {cbind(c(.[1:12,1], .[13:24,1] / -0.5 + 12), .[,2])}
```

We would expect the edges to be plotted in order (from top to bottom in the dataframe/tidygraph), however, we see that the ninth edge is actually on top (this is true regardless of the naming convention).

``` r
# does not work
ggraph(g, layout=layout) +
  geom_edge_link(aes(colour=z, label=z), width=3)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/SRcQLOt.png)<!-- -->

`geom_edge_link0` seems to work, as does manually setting the group variable to be the same for all edges, so I suspect it has to do with assigning the group variable on line 197 of [`geom_edge_link.R`](https://github.com/thomasp85/ggraph/blob/main/R/geom_edge_link.R).

``` r
# works!
ggraph(g, layout=layout) +
  geom_edge_link0(aes(colour=z), width=3)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/sKAY53H.png)<!-- -->

``` r
# works!
ggraph(g, layout=layout) +
  geom_edge_link(aes(colour=z, label=z, group=I(1)), width=3)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/FhbmLLo.png)<!-- -->

The order of plotting is reminiscent of the order you get when sorting an integer range that has been converted to a character:

``` r
1:12 %>% as.character() %>% sort()
#>  [1] "1"  "10" "11" "12" "2"  "3"  "4"  "5"  "6"  "7"  "8"  "9"
```

and, indeed, considering the number of edges up to 100, the 99th edge is plotted last:

``` r
a <- 100
g <- tbl_graph(edges=tibble(from=1:a, to=(a+1):(2*a)), directed=FALSE) %E>%
  mutate(z=1:n()) %N>%
  mutate(type=c(rep(TRUE, a), rep(FALSE, a)))
layout <- igraph::layout_as_bipartite(g) %>%
  {cbind(c(.[1:a,1], .[(a+1):(2*a),1] / -0.5 + a), .[,2])}
ggraph(g, layout=layout, ncol=2) +
  geom_edge_link(aes(colour=(z==99), label=z), width=3)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/YuuUocp.png)<!-- -->

<sup>Created on 2023-12-08 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

title: geom_circle() ignoring linewidth parameter
description:
Hi! 

I've just found out that when modifying the width of the lines in `geom_circle()`, the `linewidth` parameter is ignored.

See, based on the example from the docs:

```
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)

circles <- data.frame(
  x0 = rep(1:3, 3),
  y0 = rep(1:3, each = 3),
  r = seq(0.1, 1, length.out = 9)
)

# Fails to change linewidth:
ggplot() +
  geom_circle(aes(x0 = x0, y0 = y0, r = r, fill = r), linewidth = 5, data = circles) +
  coord_fixed()

# A warning message is returned:
# Warning message:
# Ignoring unknown parameters: linewidth

```
![irudia](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41082643/190650603-0e77641f-2daa-4015-b049-0455a9df4b19.png)


However, if `size` is provided instead of `linewidth`, the line width is changed:

```
ggplot() +
  geom_circle(aes(x0 = x0, y0 = y0, r = r, fill = r), size = 5, data = circles) +
  coord_fixed()
```
![irudia](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41082643/190650715-78614ea7-4fa7-46f5-8177-d323b24189f4.png)


From the documentation I understand that the intended behaviour should be providing the line width via the `linewidth` aesthetic, not `size` (which is not mentioned in the docs). `lineend` is also ignored. All other aesthetics seem to behave just fine.

I hope it is of help!

title: Shrink has no effect when combining facet_zoom and geom_ribbon?
description:
Strong possibility I am misunderstanding what the `shrink = TRUE` option is meant to do, but I would expect the y-axis on the zoomed plot to be rescaled in the following reprex?

``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)
library(matrixStats)

x_vals <- seq(from = 0, to = 1, length.out = 100)
y_vals <- 2 + 1.2 * x_vals
y_data <- matrix(NA, ncol = 100, nrow = 500)
y_data[] <- y_vals
y_data <- y_data + rnorm(n = prod(dim(y_data)), sd = 0.1) 

plot_df <- data.frame(
  x = x_vals,
  y = rowMeans(y_data),
  y_true = y_vals,
  lowers = rowQuantiles(y_data, probs = 0.25),
  uppers = rowQuantiles(y_data, probs = 0.75)
)

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = x)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = y_true)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lowers, ymax = uppers), alpha = 0.2) +
  facet_zoom(xlim = c(0.45, 0.55), shrink = TRUE)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/hRposez.png)

<sup>Created on 2019-03-11 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.1.9000)</sup>

Testing suggests that `shrink` has no effect here, so I'm slightly confused about its intended effect.

title: geom_spiro not animatable
description:
This "pretty useless" geom probably isn't at the top of the list of bugs to fix, but I thought I would put it out there that I can't get geom_spiro from ggforce to animate. Tried transition_time, transition_components, and transition_states but all three throw the error:
`Error in mapply(FUN = f, ..., SIMPLIFY = FALSE) : 
  zero-length inputs cannot be mixed with those of non-zero length`

Seems to be related to thomasp85/gganimate#139 and thomasp85/gganimate#196, probably geom_spiro is overwriting the group aesthetic which makes gganimate mad. 

Here's a reprex

```
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)
library(gganimate)

data <- data.frame(R = c(2, 3), r = c(1, 1), d = c(3, 2), id = c(1, 2))

#works
p <-
  ggplot(data) +
  geom_spiro(aes(R = R, r = r, d = d, group = id))

#doesnt work
p + transition_time(time = id)
p + transition_components(time = id)
p + transition_states(states = id)
```

title: facet_zoom won't zoom in xlim/ylim if axis limit set before (like in y_scale_continuous)
description:
facet_zoom is a great feature but surely challenging to implement... 
If ylim or xlim is set in the parent plot, it won't work to further set ylim or xlim in the zoom-in plot. The zoom in range will just follow the setting before. This is not a big issue though, just a notice. 
It might relate to issue #133 for the same reason.
I searched if there is a way to cross it in ggplot but haven't found a solution. I appreciate any advice.
```
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)
ggplot(iris, aes(Petal.Length, Petal.Width, colour = Species)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,2)) +
  facet_zoom(ylim = c(0,1), horizontal = F)
```
same for:
```
ggplot(iris, aes(Petal.Length, Petal.Width, colour = Species)) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0,2)) +
  facet_zoom(ylim = c(0,1), horizontal = F)

title: Feature Request: Allow geom_text to Follow a Line Segment
description:
As discussed in tidyverse/ggplot2#2852, would it be reasonable to extract the geom_text along a line segment feature from ggraph to a generalized solution in ggforce?

I *think* that the process would be porting https://github.com/thomasp85/ggraph/blob/master/R/textAlong.R along with some bits from https://github.com/thomasp85/ggraph/blob/master/R/geom_edge.R to ggforce.  But, maybe I'm missing something (likely as I've not written a Geom before).

title: geom_circle() fails if aes(x = [something],  y=[something_else]) is included.
description:
Hi, 
Thank you for your many great packages!

I think there is a bug in geom_circle()
The error seems to come when if aes( x = [something], y = [something_else]) is included in the starting call to ggplot:

Library and data:

```
library(tidyverse)
library(ggforce)

person <- tribble(
  ~object,    ~x,    ~y,   ~group, ~size,
  "head",      100,   180,      1,    10, 
  "neck",      100,   160,      1,    3, 
  "pelvis",    100,   100,      1,    3, 
  "lhip",       90,    90,      2,    3, 
  "rhip",      110,    90,      3,    3,
  "lknee",      80,    45,      2,    3,
  "rknee",     120,    45,      3,    3, 
  "lfoot",      50,     0,      2,    3, 
  "rfoot",      150,    0,      3,    3,
  "lshoulder",   85,  155,      4,    3, 
  "rshoulder",  115,  155,      5,    3, 
  "lhand",      75,   100,      4,    3, 
  "rhand",      125,  100,      5,    3)
```


This works:
```
plot_x_y_aes_below <- ggplot(person, aes(x0=x, y0=y, r=size, group=group, fill=factor(group), color=factor(group))) +
  geom_circle(fill = "black") +
  geom_point(aes(x,y))+
  geom_path(aes(x,y)) +
  coord_equal() + 
  labs(x="cm", y="cm") + 
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

plot_x_y_aes_below
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40394828/59256448-437d8b80-8c34-11e9-8a4a-9fecd4525ba8.png)

If we move aes(x,y) from geom_point and geom_path to the top:
```
plot_x_y_aes_on_top <- ggplot(person, aes(x = x, y = y, x0=x, y0=y, r=size, group=group, fill=factor(group), color=factor(group))) +
  geom_circle(fill = "black") +
  geom_point()+
  geom_path() +
  coord_equal() + 
  labs(x="cm", y="cm") + 
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

plot_x_y_aes_on_top
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40394828/59256521-6dcf4900-8c34-11e9-94c1-9e6b927c2e9b.png)

Having played around with this I think the error is that the data becomes distorted (by a factor of ~2.5), and the "r" argument is ignored so the circle size becomes minimal. 
This becomes more clear if we manually override the r argument by setting the size argument.
*Perhaps also of interest, the fill argument is ignored, it is behaving like a point*
```
plot_x_y_aes_on_top_manuel_size <- ggplot(person, aes(x = x, y = y, x0=x, y0=y, r=size, group=group, fill=factor(group), color=factor(group))) +
  geom_circle(fill = "black", size = 5) +
  geom_point()+
  geom_path() +
  coord_equal() + 
  labs(x="cm", y="cm") + 
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

plot_x_y_aes_on_top_manuel_size
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40394828/59256889-2c8b6900-8c35-11e9-9f07-ae3fba1d71ea.png)

If I remove the geom_poin() the error is the same (see below). I therefore think the error comes from placing aes(x = [something], y = [something_else]) in the first call to ggplot.

```
plot_x_y_aes_on_top_manuel_size_no_geom_point <- ggplot(person, aes(x = x, y = y, x0=x, y0=y, r=size, group=group, fill=factor(group), color=factor(group))) +
  geom_circle(fill = "black", size = 5) +
  geom_path() +
  coord_equal() + 
  labs(x="cm", y="cm") + 
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

plot_x_y_aes_on_top_manuel_size_no_geom_point
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/40394828/59257091-90159680-8c35-11e9-9d0b-51ef7cb8e1bc.png)

I hope this can help.

title: Add geom_bar_arc() feature to another plot
description:
Dear Thomas,

Thank you so much for your force and what you do with it - ggforce is one of the best things I encountered in R so far! I would like to use geom_bar_arc() as an annotation tool since I need round shapes and neither geom_rect() nor geom_segment() fulfill my needs. I have a donut plot (created with sunburst() from ggsunburst package) and as the outermost layer I would like to have 3 arcs to annotate the donut plot.

data.frame for sunburst plot
```
df_size <- read.table(header=FALSE, text = "
parent,node,timepoint,size
controls,normal,3.5h,100.00
controls,normal,24h,88.23
controls,SCV,24h,11.76
controls,normal,48h,72.09
controls,SCV,48h,27.91
samples,SCV,48h,36.04
samples,normal,48h,64.00
samples,SCV,24h,33.02
samples,normal,24h,67.00
samples,normal,3.5h,100.00")
```

data.frame for arcs
```
tp <- data.frame(
  time_point = c('3.5h', '24h', '48h', '24h'),
  start = c(5.235988, 1.047198, 2.094395, 4.18879),
  end = c(1.047198, 2.094395, 4.18879, 5.235988),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```
create sunburst plot featuring geom_arc_bar()
```
write.table(df_size,"df_size.csv", col.names = F, row.names = F, sep=",")
sb_size <- sunburst_data("df_size.csv", type="node_parent", sep=",", node_attributes = c("timepoint", "size"))
sunburst(sb_size, leaf_labels = F, node_labels = T, node_labels.min = 70, rects.fill.aes = "name") +
  scale_fill_discrete(guide=F) +
  geom_text(data = sb_size$leaf_labels, aes(x=x, y=y, label=paste(timepoint, size, sep="\n"))) +
  geom_arc_bar(aes(x0 =0, y0 =12, r0 =1, r = 3, start=start, end=end, fill = time_point), data = tp)
```
With the code above I get the following:
![grafik](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/45228113/60653022-843e7e00-9e49-11e9-92d1-84aaaa3e9851.png)
I would like to have the arcs around the plot to better visualize the 3 timepoints 3.5h, 24h and 48h. I do get both plots but somehow I am missing the 3.5h arc and I don't manage to set the coordinates right. There is no negative y0 coordinate and also, the arcs do not form a proper circle. Do you know 
a) how I get my 5.235988 to 1.047198 radians arc back?
b) how I can set the coordinates for the geom_arc_bar() to fall around the donut plot AND make it properly circular?
c) how to make the geom_arc_bar() coordinates independent from the sunburst coordinates?

Question c) is because the plot looks like this when I comment the geom_arc_bar() line out.
![plot_zoom_1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/45228113/60653325-1e9ec180-9e4a-11e9-984d-5c103f858366.png)
So here the issue is that the rescaling of the sunburst plot is difficult once I add the geom_arc_bar() layer. In the plot above, you also see that the arcs squeeze into the sunburst plot, depending on the y0 value. 

### Thanks for your help!
May the force be with you,
Tse

title: Allow facet_matrix() to take a labeller argument

title: facet_zoom fails on grouped input data
description:
Found this out when trying to use `facet_zoom` on what I thought was a very simple table. `facet_zoom` doesn't appear to ignore grouping on the input data, which causes it to throw an error that seems to be from `cbind_all`. Using the readme example, to show it works fine without grouping:

library(dplyr)

  geom_point() +
  facet_zoom(x = Species == "setosa")

title: Problem  with facet_grid_paginate()
description:
I am trying to produce a ggplot2 graphic in which there is a single conditioning variable with a large number of levels (24).

If I use facet_grid() I get a plot with either 24 rows or 24 columns,
both of which look like hell.

I thought that facet_grid_paginate() would rescue me, but it doesn't seem to.  I asked for 3 rows and 4 columns, and thought that I would get two 3 x 4 pages  Instead I get six pages with only one row (of four facets) per page.

Am I misunderstanding something?  Making some silly syntactical error?  Or is this a bug?

I have attached a reproducible example, along with the data set on which it depends.

Grateful for any insight.

P.S.  Someone suggested to me that I could use facet_wrap() from ggplot2 instead. title: geom_spiro - edge correction for revolutions
description:
Hi Thomas,

I am using ggforce_0.3.2 and ggplot2_3.3.2 and use geom_spiro. The created plots will result in an sharp edge at the starting and endpoint of the path. 

``` r,
ggplot() +
  geom_spiro(
    aes(
      R = 13,
      r = 3,
      d = 3,
      outer = TRUE
    )
  ) +
  theme_void()
```
[spiro_revo_null.pdf](https://github.com/thomasp85/ggforce/files/5523562/spiro_revo_null.pdf)

In contrast, setting the parameter `revolutions` to a value greater than the internally calculated `revo` will solve the issue.

```r,
ggplot() +
  geom_spiro(
    aes(
      R = 13,
      r = 3,
      d = 3,
      outer = TRUE
    ), 
    revolutions = 4 
  ) +
  theme_void()
```
[spiro_revo_4.pdf](https://github.com/thomasp85/ggforce/files/5523575/spiro_revo_4.pdf)

Therefore, I suggest that changing the default behaviour of geom_spiro, in terms of calculating 'revo', could be of help.

```r,
if (is.null(revolutions)) {
      revo <- attr(fractions(data$r / data$R), 'fracs')
      revo <- as.numeric(sub('/.*$', '', revo))
      revo <- revo + 1
    }
```

Best regards, Philipp

title: scale_y_unit with trans gives wrong axis title
description:
I'm really happy that these scales exist, but unfortunately there are some problems that may or may not arise from this. I have been trying to investigate but I could not find out where exactly this is due to a more upstream bug, or if it originates here.

I hope it is something simple to address, since the units package is very useful, and I'd really like to use it in ggplot2.

```library(units)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)

# Just some example data with exponential numbers in the y axis
example_data <- data.frame(x = set_units(1:100, m), y = set_units(exp(1:100), m))

# This plots correctly
ggplot(example_data, aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_point()

# Here the plot is correct, as well as the bins, but the axis title is 
# y[lg(re 1 m)]
# which should be just y [m]
#

ggplot(example_data, aes(x=x, y=y)) + scale_y_unit(trans="log10") + geom_point()

# Interestingly, using the units parameter removes the trans, but also the breaks so there is only the axis title
# With the following command the axis title is y[cm]

ggplot(example_data, aes(x=x, y=y)) + scale_y_unit(trans="log10", unit = "cm") + geom_point()```

title: support tidyselect in gather_set_data()

```r
d = tibble(
  amount = rnorm(20, 100, 20),
  t_1 = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 20, TRUE), 
  t_2 = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 20, TRUE), 
  t_3 = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 20, TRUE)
)

# works
gather_set_data(d, 2:4)
gather_set_data(d, names(d)[2:4])

gather_set_data(d, vars(matches("t_")))
```

title: Ordering of shapes is changed by `arcPaths`
description:
This was reported on StackOverflow here:  https://stackoverflow.com/q/66408402/2554330 .  The following
code plots the circles in the wrong order, so the overlaps look wrong:
``` r
library(tidyverse)
library(ggforce)

circles <- data.frame(
    x0 = seq(1, 30),
    y0 = seq(1, 30),
    r = 2
)

ggplot() +
    geom_circle(aes(x0 = x0, y0 = y0, r = r), fill = "grey", data = circles) +
    coord_fixed()
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/9X9fY7f.png)

<sup>Created on 2021-02-28 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

The problem is that `arcPaths` uses `base::make.unique()` to construct group names for the shapes, and it doesn't preserve the original ordering.  I'll submit a PR.

title: geom_sina produces inaccurate values
description:
geom_sina introduces a nontrivial amount of y jitter (aka inaccuracy in plotted data values). 

**See this reprex:**
library(ggforce)
a=c(1,2,3,4,5); b=c(1,1,1,1,1); 
data=tibble(a=a,b=b); 
ggplot(data,aes(x=b,y=a)) + geom_sina()

I have not been able to find a way to turn this off. 
Is there a way? 
Even if it is possible to turn off, I think it is better to have the default behavior be accurate data values. 

The sinaplot function in the sinaplot package does not do this. 

**See this reprex:**
library(sinaplot)
sinaplot(c(1,2,3,4,5))

Thank you for all the amazing functions in ggforce. 
They are just wonderful and much appreciated!

title: facet_zoom throws "subscript out of bounds" if x/y expressions include no data
description:
```r
xs <- tibble(x=1:10, y=1:10)
ggplot(xs, aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_point() + facet_zoom(x < 5)
# Obviously, this works.
ggplot(xs, aes(x=x, y=y)) + geom_point() + facet_zoom(x < 0)
# Error in scale_index[[i]] : subscript out of bounds
```

The `x < 0` in `facet_zoom` subsets no data, and this seems to throw an error.

The previous example is obviously trivial. But this error also appears when the facet_zoom x/y expression does subset from the full data as given in the ggplot call, but does not subset from an "overwriting" geom-specific data.

For example, suppose I want to label just outliers with geom_text.

```r
xs <- tibble(x=1:10, y=c(1:9, 100))
ggplot(xs, aes(x=x, y=y, label=y)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_text(data=filter(xs, y > 50)) +
  facet_zoom(x<10)
# Error in scale_index[[i]] : subscript out of bounds

# But this works
ggplot(xs, aes(x=x, y=y, label=y)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_text(data=filter(xs, y <= 50)) +
  facet_zoom(x<10)
```

For other users coming across this issue, one fix is to use xlim/ylim instead of x/y expressions (#221).

title: `geom_sina()` removes all data points when colouring by discrete variable
description:
I am trying to plot a small number of data points and colour them by a third variable. The x-axis as well as the colouring variable are discrete, while the y-axis is continuous. The reason I want to use `geom_sina()` is because the values can be almost identical, leading to overlapping points. I'd like the points to dodge, but only when their y value is similar. I know that `geom_beeswarm()` works, but development of ggbeeswarm has stagnated  and I'd like to explore other options.

This might be related to #268, since in my dataset every combination of `category` and `replicate` only has one data point.

What troubleshooting I've done:
- omitting `colour = replicate` results in the correct plotting of the points
- moving mapping to the `geom_sina()` function call (unsurprisingly) does not fix this issue
- using `geom_point()` instead of `geom_sina()` works as expected
- converting `replicate` to numeric fixes the issue, but now the colour scale is continuous instead of discrete (I'd like to use `scale_colour_manual()`)

Here's a reprex that closely mimics my conditions:
``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)
library(tibble)

dat <- tibble(
  category = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), 3),
  value = 1:9,
  replicate = rep(1:3, each = 3)|> as.character()
)
dat
#> # A tibble: 9 × 3
#>   category value replicate
#>   <chr>    <int> <chr>    
#> 1 A            1 1        
#> 2 B            2 1        
#> 3 C            3 1        
#> 4 A            4 2        
#> 5 B            5 2        
#> 6 C            6 2        
#> 7 A            7 3        
#> 8 B            8 3        
#> 9 C            9 3

dat |> ggplot(aes(category, value, colour = replicate)) +
  geom_sina()
#> Warning: Removed 9 rows containing missing values (geom_point).
```

title: Horizontal sina support
description:
`geom_sina()` works fine if x is the categorical covariate, and y is numeric. However, if y is categorical and x is numeric, it fails, while we can still draw box/violin plots.

```r
library(ggforce)
ggplot(midwest, aes(state, area)) +
  geom_violin() +
  geom_sina()
# Works

ggplot(midwest, aes(area, state)) +
  geom_violin() +
  geom_sina()
# Warning messages:
# 1: In regularize.values(x, y, ties, missing(ties), na.rm = na.rm) :
#   collapsing to unique 'x' values
# 2: Computation failed in `stat_sina()`:
#   need at least two non-NA values to interpolate 
# Draws violin plot, but not sina plot
```

We can overcome this limitation by flipping plots with `coord_flip()`, however, it would be really nice if we didn't have to. Especially when working with multiple packages, it can be nice to specify x and y as you want them displayed, and not flipping the plot at the end.

Alternatively, we can use the ggbeeswarm package, which has a `groupOnX` parameter to determine whether to group on the X or Y axis, and can draw similar plots, but comes with a slightly different set of options.

title: geom_circle() in combination with geom_point()
description: Hello I wanted to plot circles and on top of them, I wanted to plot a cross in the center of the circles. Since geom_circle inherits the aesthetics, I thought I could go about it this way: `circles <- data.frame( x0 = rep(1:3, 3), y0 = rep(1:3, each = 3), r = seq(0.1, 1, length.out = 9) ) ggplot() + geom_circle(aes(x0 = x0, y0 = y0, r = r, fill = r), data = circles) ggplot(data = circles, aes(x = x0, y = y0)) + geom_circle(aes(x0 = x0, y0 = y0, r = r, fill = r)) + coord_fixed() + geom_point(shape = 3)` however, this leads to this result: After some fiddling around, I found the solution: if the aesthetics of the point are specified within geom_point() itself, I get the expected result. `ggplot(data = circles) + geom_circle(aes(x0 = x0, y0 = y0, r = r, fill = r)) + coord_fixed() + geom_point(aes(x = x0, y = y0), shape = 3)` gives: I just put it up here in case anybody runs into the same trouble. Otherwise thanks for the great package!

title: Two-sided geom_diagonal_wide()?
description:
This is a new feature request, for a two-sided version of geom_diagonal_wide(). Due respect to your time, I can prototype it, but I thought you may have considered something similar for your parallel sets plots.

In the special case of an `NA` for one factor, some Sankey plots render an arc that skips that factor (except no arc in this example):
![R graph gallery Sankey plot](https://www.r-graph-gallery.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/12/322_Sankey_Change_color_node-300x300.png)

Related question: how do you see others extending ggforce? Through external packages, or contributing PR, or combination?

I really love `geom_diagonal_wide()`, especially the way it renders consistently when resizing a plot window or transforming the x-axis. I started using it for a plot type I'm developing, and I think it's fantastic.
![Two adjacent geoms, no outline](https://jmw86069.github.io/splicejam/articles/create-a-sashimi-plot_files/figure-html/plot_test_junc-1.png)

Another example with slight outline and label:
![Two adjacent geoms, slight outline](https://jmw86069.github.io/splicejam/articles/create-a-sashimi-plot_files/figure-html/plot_sashimi_gr-1.png)
The outline really helps except for the middle line.

### The main goals:

1. remove the outline in the middle of the arc, while still being able to outline the arc overall
2. position the middle of the arc at the midpoint between left and right edges (secondary goal)
3. define how high to draw the arc in the middle (differs from standard Sankey plots)

### Bonus points:

4. optionally label the arc, otherwise determining where to add a label is tricky

Aside: I got the `geom_diagonal_wide()` to render using `ggplotly()`, and it looks great!

title: facet_zoom with different data and different plot
description:
Is it possible to have zoomed region to have different Y values and different type of plot?

Example:
```R
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)

#dummy data
set.seed(1)
df1 <- data.frame(x = 1:100, y = runif(100), zoom = c(rep("a", 30), rep("b", 20), rep("c", 50)))
df2 <- data.frame(x = 1:100, y = runif(100, 1, 10))

ggplot(df1, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() + 
  facet_zoom(x = zoom == "b")
```
![plot1](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5212915/22973630/68dc032e-f376-11e6-9eef-2e964a9ecb1f.jpeg)

All great but this is not what I want. I need to have the zoomed region to have plot based on different data as Y value, and different plot type:
```R
gg1 <- ggplot(df1, aes(x, y)) + geom_point()
gg2 <- ggplot(df2, aes(x, y)) + geom_line()

#interseting area zoomed in with line plot
range(df1[ df1$zoom == "b", "x"])
# [1] 31 50
gg2zoom <- ggplot(df2[ df2$x >= 31 & df2$x <= 50, ], aes(x, y)) + 
  geom_line()

#merge plot vertically
cowplot::plot_grid(gg1, gg2zoom, nrow = 2)
```
![plot2](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5212915/22973662/84609a60-f376-11e6-9f3c-e69b3ab6d3e9.jpeg)

I would want above plot with your type of shading to show zooming area, here is expected output with bit of Paintburshing:

![plot3](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5212915/22973671/8f1d78a6-f376-11e6-89e8-f01e099a764d.jpg)

Possible? Maybe other workarounds?

title: When overlapping geom_link2, width aesthetic does not scale similarly
description:
This is a report following up on [this stackoverflow question](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/66187022/how-to-add-edges-borders-to-the-links-in-geom-link2-in-r-follow-up-question/66196486#66196486)

It seems odd to the OP, and also to me, that the width of the links does not seem to be similarly scaled... 

The issue arises from an attempt to create borders around `geom_link2` - if there should be other, better, geoms for that purpose, very very happy for a suggestion.
``` r
library(ggforce)
#> Loading required package: ggplot2
df <- data.frame( x = c(5, 10, 5, 10), y = c(5, 10, 10, 5), width = c(1, 10, 6, 2), colour = letters[1:4], group = c(1, 1, 2, 2), width_border = c(2, 11, 7, 3))
ggplot(df) +
  geom_link2(aes(x = x, y = y,  group = group, size = width_border), lineend = 'round') +
  geom_link2(aes(x = x, y = y, colour = colour, group = group, size = width), lineend = 'round', n = 500)
```

description:
Whenever I try to plot rectangles (via geom_rect()) that spans outside of the zoom area, it is ignored by facet_zoom() and gives `"Error in scale_index[[i]] : subscript out of bounds"` error. Here is the reproducible example:

```
ggplot() +
  geom_point(data= mutate(iris, zoom=T), 
             aes(Petal.Length, Petal.Width, colour = Species)) +
  geom_rect(data = data.frame(start=2, stop=6), 
            aes(xmin=start, xmax=stop, ymin=1, ymax=2)) +
  facet_zoom(x = Species == 'versicolor')
```
How can I show spanning geom_rect() elements in facet_zoom()?

title: Feature Request: geom_points colored by density
description:
_(Originally proposed for in ggplot2 as issue [3150](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/3150))_

One geom/stat which would be very useful is a hybrid between geom_density_2d and geom_point, where points are colored by their density. This would help avoid overcome overplotting by mapping the density to the color aesthetic, while preserving the individual points in areas of low density. This type of visualization is very common in flow cytometry, but could be useful elsewhere as well.

@slowkow has an excellent example of how to achieve the desired effect [here](https://slowkow.com/notes/ggplot2-color-by-density/), but it requires computing the density at each point prior to plotting, which becomes burdensome for faceted plots.

I was able to modify the `stat_density_2d` function slightly using @slowkow's code as a guide to make a new `stat_density_point_2d` function which worked well in my hands(example below), but I had trouble writing the corresponding geom. Is this something that could be considered for inclusion in ggforce?

I'd be happy to contribute my version, thought there may be a better way to achieve the same goal. 

Thanks for your consideration!
```r
library(ggplot2)
dat <- data.frame(
  x = c(
    rnorm(1e4, mean = 0, sd = 0.1),
    rnorm(1e3, mean = 0, sd = 0.1)
  ),
  y = c(
    rnorm(1e4, mean = 0, sd = 0.1),
    rnorm(1e3, mean = 0.1, sd = 0.2)
  )
)

ggplot(dat, aes(x, y)) +
  stat_identity() +
  scale_color_viridis_c() +
  theme_classic()
```

![stat_identity](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22528952/52978301-49eeab80-3396-11e9-9e60-9efcbf1d7261.png)
 
```r
ggplot(dat, aes(x, y)) +
   stat_density_point_2d() +
   scale_color_viridis_c() +
   theme_classic()
 ```
 
 ![stat_density_point_2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22528952/52978304-53781380-3396-11e9-92f5-3f76984afb0f.png)

title: Combining facet_zoom with geom_histogram
description: I wonder about feasibility of enhanced support for geom_histogram in future? Specifically the question of applying either a specific different `binwidth` to the zoomed facet, or by applying the same `bin` argument. The current implementation seems to zoom the post-binned summary: ``` set.seed(0) x = tibble(date = as.Date('2018-01-01') + rnorm(500, sd=3)^3) p = x %>% ggplot(aes(date)) + geom_histogram(bins = 50, col = 'white', size=.1) + theme_light() p + facet_zoom(x = date >= "2017-12-01" & date <= "2018-02-01", zoom.size = 1) ``` It would be really useful to be able to drill into histograms to explore spikes and strange distributions.

title: geom_circle flip when setting axis
description:
When using geom-circle to draw circles, and then setting the limits of the axis could lead to  artefacts of the circle instead of just cutting it at the plot edge.

```
library("ggplot2")
library("ggforce")

ROI=data.frame(X=c(274, 425, 925, 770, 310, 895, 10),
               Y=c(524, 680, 255,  75, 630, 120, 250),
               R=c(100, 100, 100, 100, 200, 200, 150))

ggplot(ROI) + 
       geom_circle(aes(x0=X, y0=Y, r=R, color='red', fill='red', alpha=.5),
                           n=720, lwd=2, show.legend=F) +
       scale_x_continuous(expand=c(0,0), limits=c(0,w)) +
       scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0,0), limits=c(0,720)) + 
       coord_equal()
```

![Circleflip](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1611619/57903357-4c489080-7833-11e9-9d71-98f9be2ce1f9.png)

Everything is fine when the axes are not set;

```

       geom_circle(aes(x0=X, y0=Y, r=R, color='red', fill='red', alpha=.5),
                           n=720, lwd=2, show.legend=F) + coord_equal()
```

title: facet_zoom with mapping
description:
Similar but different to #56. With [`geom_sf()`](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/tree/sf) on its way to `ggplot2` it would be great to have projection-aware `facet_zoom`ing. Part of this would likely require that the original and zoomed panels not necessarily be the same height/width, in order to maintain projections. For example, it would be great to be able to zoom a region of a map

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(maps)
library(ggplot2) 
library(ggforce) 
aus_map <- map_data("world") %>% 
  filter(region == "Australia", 
         is.na(subregion) | subregion %in% c("Tasmania", "Kangaroo Island"))
p <- ggplot() + 
  geom_polygon(aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group), 
               colour = NA, 
               data = aus_map) 
p + facet_zoom(xlim = c(131, 148), ylim = c(-45, -32), 
               zoom.size = 4)
```

![](http://i.imgur.com/1kxsFca.png)


Attempting to do similar with the `sf` branch of `ggplot2` just produces the unzoomed map in both panels and seems to miss the zoom highlight, though it certainly looks neater.

``` r
library(sf)      
library(maps)
library(ggplot2) # devtools::install_github("tidyverse/ggplot2@sf") ## NOTE sf branch
library(ggforce)
world1 <- sf::st_as_sf(map('world', plot = FALSE, fill = TRUE))
ggplot() + 
  geom_sf(data = world1) + 
  coord_sf(xlim = c(110, 160), ylim = c(-45, -10)) + 
  facet_zoom(xlim = c(132, 148), ylim = c(-45, -32))
```

![](http://i.imgur.com/1zq3GYJ.png)

This has potential to look really awesome if the unzoomed panel could have its height adjusted to maintain projection (width can currently be somewhat manually adjusted via `zoom.size`) and if the subsetting was compatible with the `sf` features (appropriate highlight/zoom).

I know it's a dev feature, so this is just 'down the track' thinking.

title: waterfall chart support (geom_waterfall or position_waterfall)
description:
I'd like to see a geom or position aesthetic for plotting waterfall charts. My primary interest is in generating cumulative histogram plots (sort of like binned empirical cumulative distribution plots) which are a special case of a waterfall plot. It is fairly straightforward to achieve waterfall plots using `geom_rect`, but the axis labeling is clunky and I don't see a good way to fake dodging for e.g. `fill` aesthetics. 

```r
df = data.frame(
  year = factor(2010:2017),
  amount = c(2000, 3400, -1100, -100, -6600, 3800, 1400, 2800)
)

df2 = df %>% 
  mutate(
    xmin = as.integer(year) - 0.5,
    xmax = as.integer(year) + 0.5,
	ymin = lag(cumsum(amount), default = 0),
	ymax = cumsum(amount)
  )

ggplot(df2) + 
  aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax) +
  geom_rect(color = "black", fill = "white") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(levels(df2$year)),
    labels = levels(df2$year))
```

It looks like this functionality has been implemented as [`position_waterfall`](https://github.com/brodieG/ggbg/blob/master/R/position-waterfall.R) in [brodieG](https://github.com/brodieG)'s unpublished [ggbg](https://github.com/brodieG/ggbg) package, so it may be easy to port this functionality.

title: new position type "stack and dodge"
description:
`ggplot2` supports positional types `"stack"` and `"dodge"` for bar/column plots.

```
library(ggplot2)
df = data.frame(
  year = rep(c("2010", "2011"), each = 4),
  treatment = rep(c("Impact", "Control")),
  type = rep(c("Phylum1", "Phylum2"), each = 2),
  total = sample(1:100, 8))
  
ggplot(df,aes(y = total,x = treatment,fill = year)) + geom_col(position="dodge")
ggplot(df,aes(y = total,x = treatment,fill = year)) + geom_col(position="stack")
```

However, I would like to simultaneously apply **both** position adjustments at once to create plots like e.g. the one below:

![](https://encrypted-tbn0.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcRDXsCqphIGqfTcQrmKqR6xzSFIwFsFIKW125detnGdkod6s2g1)

Is this something that `ggforce` could achieve, either through a new `position_` aesthetic or through a new geometry (e.g. `geom_offset_bar` or `geom_offset_col`)?

This functionality has been [requested before](https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2/issues/2267) but the `ggplot2` developers are not planning to implement such a feature.

title: stat_sina() doesn't match geom_violin()
description:
When using `stat_sina()` together with `geom_violin()`, it routinely happens that points fall outside the violins. This is the case because `stat_sina()` uses a different algorithm to calculate densities than does `geom_violin()`. I'm not quite sure why it does that; to me the `stat_sina()` code looks overly complex. We just need to calculate the density outline exactly like ggplot2 does, turn it into an interpolating function, and then use that function to jitter individual points. The result is a perfect match.

``` r
library(ggplot2)
set.seed(1234)

# ggforce implementation
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Length)) +
  geom_violin() +
  ggforce::stat_sina()
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/h0gt4bb.png)

``` r

# alternative implementation that matches
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Length)) +
  geom_violin() +
  dviz.supp::stat_sina()
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/lJNKY4j.png)

<sup>Created on 2019-02-21 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.1)</sup>

The code for my alternative implementation can be seen here:
https://github.com/clauswilke/dviz.supp/blob/master/R/stat_sina.R

It is virtually identical to `stat_ydensity()` from ggplot2. It also uses one unexported function from ggplot2, but that could be copied and pasted into the ggforce code.

title: geom_sina acts differently than geom_jitter or geom_violin with distribution of ints
description:
I think this is intended behavior, but it seems like a missed opportunity?  When distribution is clustered on the y axis, as in a distribution of ints, geom_jitter shifts some points vertically as well as horizontally. geom_violin also "spreads" the values at each point so that one can see the distribuiton.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggforce)

# create int version of area
midwest$area_ints <- (midwest$area * 100) %>% floor()

ggplot(midwest, aes(state, area_ints)) +

  geom_violin() + geom_sina()

title: Dependency on the `units` package
description: Right now, `ggforce` depends on the `units` package. It is nice that `ggforce` supports units, but depending on the package rather than suggesting it might not be the best idea. The `units` package depends on the `udunits2` package that isn't necessarily easy to install. Making `units` a suggested package rather than included might be better -- then people who do not use `units` won't have to install it and jump through the loops it take to install `udunits2` (which isn't just `install.packages(...)`).

title: Add wrapper to generate all pages with facet_wrap_paginate
description:
I believe the only tricky thing is calculating the correct total number of pages. This should be possible with `nrow`, `ncol` and `drop`. Are there other considerations that affect the total number of pages?

Once that's done, the rest is pretty straightforward. I have something like:

```
lapply(1:number_of_pages, function(i) {
    g + facet_wrap_paginate(facets, nrow, ncol, drop, ..., page = i)
  }
)
```

This returns a list where each element is a page. 

I have a few thoughts/questions before I move forward:

1. Is a list an OK format for the object to be returned?
1. The other function that works similarly is `facet_grid_paginate`, but because the number of pages is calculated differently and the actual function call to `facet_wrap_paginate` is just a small part of this function, I wouldn't bother writing generalizable function that is applied to both.
1. This takes a ggplot object as an argument, which by my reckoning is the best way to flexibly use this function.

title: `maxwidth` not working as expected in `stat_sina`
description: I've run into some problems with the `maxwidth` option in `geom_sina`. There are some scenarios where the points aren't distributed as far out along the x direction as I would expect. Consider this plot: ``` library(ggjoy) # for lincoln_weather dataset ggplot(lincoln_weather, aes(x = Month, y = `Mean Temperature [F]`)) + geom_violin(color = "transparent", fill = "gray90") + stat_sina() + theme_bw() ``` The points are not spread out at all. Setting `maxwidth = 1` has no discernible effect (though setting `maxwidth = 0` will remove all jittering, so the parameter is doing something). I looked through the code and found some lines that seem relevant, but I can't fully pinpoint what exactly the problem is. First, `maxwidth` is internally limited to 0.96: I think that's an unnecessary limit, because there may be scenarios where users might reasonably want a higher width, for example when distributions don't overlap much in the y range but some are highly peaked. Second, there is some check that seems relevant, though I can't figure out whether the if and else paths do anything different at all. It looks to me like they don't:

title: geom_sf()
description:
(Copied from [here](https://github.com/edzer/sfr/issues/88))

We need a `geom_sf()` to render simple feature objects in ggplots, e.g. where
```
nc = st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package="sf"))
ggplot() + geom_sf(nc)
```
would add the polygon boundaries, and further argument can alter the color of polygons and polygon boundaries, as well as point and line geometries. I wrote some building blocks, basically functions that convert `sf` objects into grid grobs [here](https://github.com/edzer/sfr/blob/master/R/grid.R) and am willing to help out, but would appreciate some help getting started from someone who's been here before: @thomasp85, @hadley, @mdsumner , @hrbrmstr?

Issues to keep in mind:
* can `geom_sf` control the aspect ratio used, such that 1 km north equals 1 km east?
* when combining with ggmap(), I think web mercator is assumed: automatically use `st_transform`?
* when combining different `geom_sf`s, can we verify that coordinate reference systems correspond?
